source_text: Apud quos propterea - dicis - non potuisse vos agere causam vestram, quia nemode rebus dubiis bene consultat, nisi qui ab odio, ira et amicitia vacuum pectus attulerit; quales non fuisse - dicis - qui de causa vestra iudicaverunt, quia prius eam coeperunt odisse quam nosse Si quis aut liberum in hominibus arbitrium, aut Deum esse nascentium conditorem dixerit, Pelagianus et Caelestianus vocatur
pass_a_gloss: Before whom propterea - you-say - not potuisse you to-do case vestram, because nemode rebus doubtful-things well deliberates, unless who from by-hatred, anger and friendship empty breast attulerit; quales not to-have-been - you-say - who about/from case/cause your iudicaverunt, because earlier her coeperunt to-hate than/which nosse if who or free in hominibus decision, or God to-be nascentium founder dixerit, Pelagian and Caelestian is-called.

lemmas.lexica: LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere
LS arbitrium=judgment, free decision; Blaise liberum arbitrium
LS conditor; Blaise God as maker from nothing

pass_b_english: We could not plead our case before those judges, because no one deliberates well about doubtful matters unless they come with a heart free from hatred, anger, and friendship. Those who judged our case were not like that: they began to hate it before they knew it.
If anyone says that human beings have free will or that God creates those who are born, they are called a Pelagian and a Caelestian.

choices.why: Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.
Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
